classification.difficultyReason: Select cosine from the horizontal distance and wire hypotenuse, then rearrange a ratio with the unknown in the denominator.

content.prompt:
A flagpole has a wire that secures it to the ground 6 m from the pole.
The wire makes an angle of $51^{\circ}$ with the ground.
Calculate the length of the wire to 1 decimal place.

spec.description: Flagpole on the left, securing wire descending to the ground attachment on the right, dashed ground segment and right-angle marker. Three dedicated diagram-label boxes remain empty, with a degree symbol in the angle box. Coordinates express the stated 51-degree geometry; no additional measurement is printed.
spec.mathematics: The horizontal distance is adjacent to the 51-degree angle; the wire is the hypotenuse. The pole is perpendicular to the ground.
spec.answerVisibility: Question figure contains empty response boxes only; completed labels appear in the solution figure.

answer.worked:
Label the horizontal distance $6\text{ m}$, the ground angle $51^{\circ}$ and the wire length $x\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos 51^{\circ}&=\frac{6}{x}\\x\cos 51^{\circ}&=6\\x&=\frac{6}{\cos 51^{\circ}}\\x&\approx 9.5\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete self-contained solution figure retaining the pole-left orientation and showing the three requested diagram labels. The acute interior angle runs counterclockwise from the wire to the leftward ground segment.
spec.mathematics: Adjacent side 6 m, angle 51 degrees, hypotenuse x m.
